layers.name: Domain
layers.description: The core business entities, enterprise logic, and base data structures. This layer must be entirely independent and not know about databases, web frameworks, or external APIs.

layers.name: Application
layers.description: Use cases, business rules, and application-specific logic. It coordinates the Domain layer but still knows nothing about UI or infrastructure.

layers.name: Presentation
layers.description: The delivery mechanism. Handles HTTP requests, GraphQL resolvers, web sockets, or CLI commands. Translates user input into Application use cases.

layers.name: Infrastructure
layers.description: Implementation details. Database connections (SQLAlchemy), external API integrations, caching (Redis), file system access, and messaging queues.

rules.reason: Application use cases orchestrate Domain entities.
Presentation layer triggers Application use cases.
Infrastructure implements interfaces defined by the Application layer.
Sometimes Presentation maps Domain entities directly (CQRS).
Infrastructure maps database rows to Domain entities.
